lesson.title: Meeting the Letter I — Our Second Vowel!
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You met your first vowel, A, last week. Today: a second vowel, I — and a whole new set of words to read!

The letter I makes a short sound: i, like at the start of 'igloo' or 'itch'. Vowels are special because almost every word needs at least one. Now try blending: /p/ /i/ /t/ — pit! And /s/ /i/ /t/ — sit! Notice how swapping the vowel A for I changes 'pat' into 'pit', and gives you a brand-new word each time.
You now know two vowels, and you've seen how swapping just one sound changes a whole word! Tomorrow we'll meet one more consonant.

objectives: Recognize and produce the short /i/ sound for the letter I
Blend I with known letters to read 'pit' and 'sit', noticing the vowel-swap pattern
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review P and the word 'pat' from yesterday.
2. Introduce I as the second vowel, contrasting its sound with A.
3. Blend p-i-t and s-i-t together, comparing to yesterday's 'pat' and last week's 'sat'.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace I, then trace and blend both new words.
5. Close by having the child swap the vowel in 'pat' to make 'pit' out loud.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one new word (pit) rather than both pit and sit in the same lesson
Ready for more: ask the child to find one more real word using the short /i/ sound they already know
The vowel-swap comparison (pat/pit, sat/sit) is the real teaching moment here — give it real time, not just a mention
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and blending activity — check that the child can produce the short /i/ sound and successfully blend both 'pit' and 'sit'.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Introducing a second vowel unlocks vowel-substitution as a genuine early-literacy insight — the same consonants, a different vowel, a completely different word — building directly on last week's single-vowel foundation.

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.
